safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not clearly state that looking at screens worsens symptoms.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to document that screens worsen symptoms omits a supportive migraine feature (photophobia/visual sensitivity) and may reduce the usefulness of the history for pattern recognition and patient self-management advice (e.g., screen avoidance/rest). This is unlikely to change urgent management or safety-critical decisions on its own.

safety_verdicts.content: More serious differential diagnoses need to be considered.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not explicitly document that more serious differential diagnoses need to be considered (though it does mention follow-up/neuro exam).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: In a new, sudden-onset unilateral headache with visual disturbance, dizziness, and vomiting, lack of explicit documentation that serious differentials (e.g., subarachnoid hemorrhage, stroke, intracranial pathology) were considered increases the risk of cognitive anchoring on “migraine” and could contribute to delayed escalation if symptoms evolve. This can adversely affect outcomes because these alternative diagnoses can be time-sensitive.
